evidence: tools/harpp-experience.py lesson audit --scope cms (575/42/3/530); two stale claims verified absent from the tree; tests tools/tests/test_lesson_effect.py 10/10, suites 58/58
reason: Owner asked what would make prose measurable like implemented things, and for a contextual review of the CMS module's prose lessons.
text: Prose becomes measurable when it names something that exists and can be checked. Grade each lesson by what it REFERENCES, not by how it reads: anchored (names a repo path that still exists -> the claim has an inspectable subject), stale (names a path that is GONE -> the claim may already be obsolete), prose (names nothing checkable -> unmeasurable until rewritten as a check). Measured on cms 2026-11-19: 42 anchored, 3 stale, 530 prose (92%), 41 of the prose being ACTIVE and injected today. Two traps found by building it: an extension alternation ordered short-first parsed 'module.json' as 'module.js' and reported every manifest as a missing javascript file (order longest-first and guard with (?![\w.])); and example paths inside fenced blocks or named my-module must be excluded or the stale bucket fills with CLI usage samples. Most damaging real finding: the genuinely stale lessons were pure FILE INVENTORIES ('src/http/*.php', 'kernel/Services/*.php') whose subjects had been deleted or refactored away - harvest produces enumerations that decay silently and nothing detects it. When auditing, verify each stale hit against the tree instead of trusting the bucket, and do not oversell 'anchored + covered': most anchored lessons are inventories too, so a test referencing the same path is not a gate waiting to be written.
